About the Role 

Imagine pioneering the mathematical and logical foundations that enable AI to fly safely in real-world, safety-critical aviation. As a Machine Learning Certification Researcher, you will address one of the most fundamental challenges in modern AI: proving that ML models are safe, reliable, and mathematically sound for deployment in autonomous flight. Your work will bridge the gap between cutting-edge statistical learning theory and formal aviation certification frameworks, building upon previous work (EASA CoDANN I and II, and FAA report DOT/FAA/TC-21/48), and putting real-world systems to the test.

At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision—developing safety-critical AI systems at the intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, understand, and make decisions in real time, we combine aerospace engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight systems, driving innovation where it matters most.

What You'll Do 

• AI Certification Strategy: Analyze our existing AI certification strategy and help adapt it—or pioneer entirely new strategies—to certify different supervised ML.

• EASA Framework Alignment: Connect mathematical guarantees, technical arguments, and model evaluations to the EASA W-shaped process for AI certification in aviation, ensuring our research aligns with the latest regulatory guidelines.

• Theoretical Foundation & Modeling: Conduct research into statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and mathematical guarantees for deep neural networks operating under dynamic real-world conditions.

• Uncertainty Quantification: Apply statistics and stochastic processes to model environmental uncertainties and sensor noise, and to quantify confidence in performance metrics.

• Literature & Proof Evaluation: Critically evaluate academic literature, mathematical proofs, and engineering assumptions with peer-review rigor to identify safety limitations and theoretical gaps in state-of-the-art AI.

• Regulatory & Audit Justification: Construct robust, logical arguments and technical justifications that translate complex, high-dimensional empirical data into structured evidence for safety audits and certification frameworks.

• Algorithmic Validation: Write clean, reproducible code in Python to test theoretical hypotheses, validate certification mechanisms, and benchmark model safety frameworks.

Requirements 

What You'll Need 

Machine Learning Theory & Mathematics 

• ML Theory & Statistical Learning: Deep understanding of statistical learning theory, generalization bounds, and the mathematical foundations of deep neural networks.

• Statistics & Stochastic Processes: Strong background in advanced probability, statistical modeling, and stochastic processes.

• Python Engineering: Proficiency in Python with the ability to write clean, reproducible code (can also be learned on the job provided strong theoretical foundations and basic Python coding).

Research Rigor 

• Scientific Research Methodology: Demonstrated capability or background in conducting comprehensive literature reviews, identifying gaps in current state-ofthe-art AI, and synthesizing complex academic concepts into actionable engineering frameworks (can also be learned on the job if you possess a strong quantitative baseline).

• Peer Review Expertise: Ability or experience in the peer-review process—capable of critically evaluating mathematical proofs, algorithmic assumptions, and research papers to assess their validity and limitations.

Education 

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s, or PhD in Computer Science, Mathematics, Theoretical Statistics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related quantitative research field.

Who You Are 

• Critical Thinking & Healthy Skepticism: You possess a strong spirit of questioning everything. You naturally challenge conventional ML assumptions, probe for hidden edge cases, and refuse to take empirical accuracy at face value without rigorous proof.

• Logical Argument Building: You have an exceptional ability to construct robust, airtight logical arguments and technical justifications. You can translate complex empirical observations into structured, defensible evidence that satisfies strict 

engineering and regulatory scrutiny.

title: Leiter Automatisierungstechnik Siemens TIA
description:
About EH Group Engineering 

EHG is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field. 

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

Key Responsibilities: 

- Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

- Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

- Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

- Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

- Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

- Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

- Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

- Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

- Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

- Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

- Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

Skills and Experience Required: 

- BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

- Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

- Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

- Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

- Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

- Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

- Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

- Proven team player, with the ability to: 
(i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team 
(ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

- Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

- Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

- Professional working language is in English.

Start date: Immediately

title: Responsable Qualité Multi-Sites - Piles à Combustible
description:
About EHG 

EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

The opportunity 

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

What you'll own 

- One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

- Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

- In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

- Supplier quality for a shared global supply base , working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

- Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

- Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites , including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

- Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

- Certification across regions , working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

- Quality culture on both floors , including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

- Building the US quality capability , defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

What we're looking for 

Core experience 

- Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

- Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

- Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

- Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

- Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

- Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

- The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

- Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling 

- Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

- Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

- Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

- Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

- Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

- Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

What we offer 

- Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

- Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

- The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

title: Robotics Integration Engineer
description:
About Enact 

The next defining technological breakthrough will be in the physical world. We stand at a historical inflection point: bringing general-purpose intelligence into robotics.

At Enact we rethink the entire robotic tech stack from model architectures and data pipelines, to the actuators and sensors that feed the model. Pushing beyond pure vision and language approaches, we build a proprioceptive nerve system, and the cortex that makes sense of it, to solve dexterity through whole-body force-awareness and deploy robots for thousands of tasks in industry and beyond.

We are shaping a company where brilliant and unconventional people thrive together on solving the hardest challenges of our time. We are truth seekers. We reason from first principles, test our beliefs against reality, and trust that the best ideas can come from anyone. We move fast. We care deeply about our work and colleagues and are driven by passion to change the status quo.

If this resonates, we're excited to hear from you.

In This Role You Will 

- Design, integrate and test the electromechanical systems at the core of our dexterous robots: actuator modules, joints, and end-effectors, sensors, PCBs, and cable harnesses into compact, reliable units for high-DoF robotics

- Bring hardware to life: lead system assembly & bring-up, debug across mechanics, electronics, and firmware, and work with controls & AI engineers to build a fully vertically integrated manipulation system

- Develop & build automated test setups to validate performance, durability, and reliability, and take systems from prototype to series production

What We're Looking For 

- Degree (BSc/MSc/PhD) in mechatronics, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field

- 3+ years of work experience developing complex mechatronic systems that bridge mechanical design, electronics, and software

- Solid understanding of electric motors, encoders, sensors, and motor drivers, and how to integrate them into a working system

- Experience with system-level debugging and testing using tools such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, logic analyzers, and data acquisition systems

- Comfortable with programming for test automation and data analysis (e.g., Python)

- Familiarity designing parts in CAD (e.g. Onshape)

- Hands-on experience with rapid prototyping, workshop tools, soldering, 3D printing, and prototype assembly/testing

- Fluency in English (spoken and written), with strong interpersonal and communication skills

Bonus Points If You Have 

- Hands-on development experience with high-DoF robotic systems (e.g., robotic arms, end-effectors, dexterous hands, or humanoids)

- Development experience with actuator systems (frameless motors, gearboxes, encoders, and integrated drives)

- Experience with motor control and communication buses such as EtherCAT or CAN

- Experience with PCB design or schematic review, and cable harness design

- Thermal management for compact, high-power electronics and actuators

What we offer 

- The opportunity to make a real impact working on some of the biggest challenges of our time

- A fast-paced learning environment alongside an outstanding, driven team

- Ownership from day one, with the ability to iterate quickly and see your impact firsthand in an early-stage startup

- Visa sponsorship & relocation benefits to hire the best in the world

- A world-class in-person setup in central Zürich, with excellent prototyping, robotics, and technical infrastructure for hands-on builders

- Competitive compensation and meaningful equity participation

From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.

Monumental is based in the city centre of Amsterdam, in a beautiful facility with an fully equipped workshop and robot testing floor. We build the whole stack in-house - hardware and software, we're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.

Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company . You might enjoy Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage , or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like .

About the role 

Monumental are already deploying robots into the real world at scale, building beautiful, bespoke homes. Our robots are on sites across the Netherlands and the UK and will be in the US within a year. Every deployment teaches us something about our hardware; you’ll push our R&D fleet to become one ready for large-series production: you'll own taking us from tens of robots a year to hundreds, and then thousands. You'll also keep that growing fleet deployable, and making design changes yourself to improve reliability and serviceability.

Scaling a fleet means solving whatever is in the way: limited space, no clear production process, lead times we can't live with and modules that don't survive the harsh conditions of a construction site. You’ll be expected to wear many hats; we’re looking for people who are genuinely excited to lead these efforts.

Our robots are built from modules at every level of maturity, so expect to work with the hardware R&D team at early stages of development to validate R&D designs as fast as we can. In parallel, you'll be in the workshop determining how we assemble them: the processes, the fixtures, the production space itself, getting the very best out of our Amsterdam facilities.

For more context on building hardware at Monumental, read Niall’s Substack: I quit my job and moved country to make robots that will fix Europe’s housing crisis. 

What you'll do 

- Bottom line, you'll own increasing our quarterly production from 30 sets of robot systems to 100 within a year. This is a challenge. You'll be building the production capabilities at Monumental rather than inheriting them, and you'll do it alongside engineers and technicians who care a great deal about getting this right.

- Take prototypes through to production-ready modules. Find and address design flaws, validate improvements, and push these modules to production.

- Assembling modules, understand the friction slowing production, and address issues yourself along with the hardware team.

- Develop fixtures, jigs and light automation solutions to support module assembly.

- Find production processes that bring minimal value when done in-house. Work with external suppliers to outsource them, while maintaining production quality.

- Produce drawings, assembly instructions and quality checks to make sure our modules are integrated together and our robots are brought up with no errors.

What we're looking for 

- Industry experience, ideally in a VC-backed start-up, transitioning products from prototype to production

- Hands-on, analytical mindset: skilled at building assemblies, running studies, analysing data, solving production and quality issues, and collaborating with technicians to implement and validate improvements

- Proficiency in mechanical assembly (press fits, fastener selection, harness, etc.)

- Strong knowledge of GD&T and producing 3D and 2D drawings

- Experience creating structured process documentation (work instructions, SOPs, quality checklists)

- Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken

Nice-to-haves 

- BSc in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing or Industrial Engineering, or equivalent

- Familiarity with robotics or complex electromechanical systems

- Experience with ERP tools (Odoo or similar)

Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. title: Growth Marketer
description:
About us: 

Tebi is creating the first Connected Restaurant Management System that makes hospitality flow. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen prep, payments, and all the data that powers it, creating smooth service and intuitive insights.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is built in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Italy, Spain, Germany, Denmark and Finland already love running on Tebi.

About the role: 

Restaurant owners generally aren't on LinkedIn and they don't read e-books. They ask friends, search Google, and more and more often, they ask ChatGPT. We need someone who can find new ways to reach them and get those ideas live quickly.

We're hiring a Growth Marketer to build and ship our organic and non-paid growth experiments. This role is for a builder, not a strategist. You'd rather ship a working test today than a polished deck next week. You'll take ideas from the backlog to live, measure them honestly, and double down on what works. Using AI and no-code tools, you'll build pages, tools and campaigns yourself instead of relying on agencies and six-figure budgets.

You'll report to the Head of Marketing, who sets direction and priorities. You'll work in deep collaboration with our other growth marketers, product marketing and creative teammates, plus embed yourself in the wider org of Sales, Account Management, RevOps, Product, and more.

What you'll be doing: 

- Ship growth experiments, fast: Take ideas from our growth backlog and get them live: landing pages, tools, ads and content. Run plenty of them, keep what works and kill what doesn't.

- Get Tebi recommended by AI: Own our visibility in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Overviews. Create and update content built to be cited, not just published, and track how often we show up compared with competitors.

- Build tools operators actually use: Build free tools, calculators and templates for restaurant owners, and scale our programmatic landing pages. Use no-code, AI and vibe coding tools to ship without waiting on engineering.

- Run creative campaigns: Help launch scrappy, unconventional campaigns across markets, from competitive campaigns to guerrilla and partner media, with the support of our Marketing team.

- Turn word of mouth into a channel: Test referral and sharing ideas that turn merchant word of mouth into a steady flow of demo requests. Work with our Product Growth team to build the winners into the product.

- Keep paid and organic working together: Support our performance agency with landing pages, creative tests and tracking.

- Measure everything: Keep the experiment log up to date: hypothesis, cost, result and next step. Set up tracking and UTMs properly so we know what actually drove each demo.

How we'll measure success: 

- Experiments shipped each month, and what we learned from them

- Demo requests from organic and other non-paid channels

- How often Tebi appears in AI answers for our category, by market

- Demos from free tools, the reservation widget and programmatic pages

What you’ll bring: 

- Think like a growth marketer but move like a hacker. You know what drives results and how to build just enough to prove it

- Ship rather than spec. A working prototype today beats a polished plan next week

- Have built and launched things yourself, like pages, tools, automations or campaigns, and can tell us what happened, including what didn't work

- Already use AI to work faster and have a point of view on how it's changing the way people find products

- Are hands-on with no-code and AI tools (Framer or Webflow, Zapier or Make, Claude or ChatGPT, Cursor or similar), without being precious about the stack

- Are comfortable with data and honest about results, in GA4, HubSpot, Looker or whatever gets the answer

- Have creative, sharp ideas and the discipline to ship the unglamorous parts too

- Take ownership and don't wait to be told what to do. No task is above or beneath you

- Speak fluent English. Another European language is a plus

Nice to have: 

- Experience with SEO, and with AEO or getting a brand cited by AI tools

- Experience marketing to small businesses, or a background in hospitality

- Vibe-coding projects you're proud of

We don't have a minimum number of years for this role. We care more about how you think and what you've built than how long you've been doing it. If this sounds like you but you don't tick every box, we'd still like to hear from you.

Benefits: 

- Start-up Equity

- Competitive Salary

- Lunch Provided in Office

- Team building events

- Unlimited time off

What is Restaurant Software? 

Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don’t. It’s a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it’s a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How we use AI at Tebi 

We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn’t make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

title: Total Rewards & People Business Partner
description:
People Business Partner & Total Rewards 

Most People roles ask you to run processes someone else built. This one asks you to build them, and to own one of them outright: how Eye rewards and recognises its people. You’ll do that while partnering the part of the business where cybersecurity actually happens, with managers who are still learning to lead and specialists who know exactly how rare they are. If you need a mature organization around you to do your best work, this isn’t it. If you get energy from building one, keep reading.

The role 

This role has two halves, and you’ll split your time roughly evenly between them.

The first half is Total Rewards. You’ll own compensation and benefits at Eye, including salary reviews, benchmarking, levelling, benefits and our equity program. There’s no finished framework waiting for you. You’ll shape it, make it hold up as we grow, and get us ready for EU pay transparency. You don’t need to be a reward specialist yet. If you owned reward projects before and want to make this your expertise, this is where you do it.

The second half is partnering. You’ll be the People Business Partner for our core business: security operations, incident response, customer support & onboarding, and project management. It’s the most varied population in the company: working students running shift rosters next to deeply specialized senior engineers, and managers at very different stages of their leadership journey.

That mix is exactly why this role needs presence more than years. You’ll coach a first-time manager on the basics one hour and align a salary band with C-level the next. You’ll need to be comfortable doing both, and to enjoy it.

What you’ll do 

- Own Total Rewards end to end: run the annual salary review, keep our benchmarks honest, and build levelling and salary bands that make sense to managers and employees alike.

- Manage benefits: run our benefits across the Netherlands, the UK, Germany and Belgium, work with providers, and keep improving what actually matters to our people.

- Manage our equity program: grants, refreshers, and making sure people understand what their equity means.

- Prepare Eye for pay transparency: work with Legal and Finance so we’re ready for the EU directive, not scrambling to catch up.

- Be the trusted partner for leaders in security operations and customer support: coaching, challenging and advising at every level of maturity, up to and including the executive team.

- Be visible. This is an office where face-to-face matters: you’ll be on the floor in The Hague, listening to what’s actually going on, not partnering from a distance.

- Handle the real side of employee relations: sick leave and reintegration, conduct issues and complex cases, working with external counsel when needed. You’ve seen the challenging cases and you don’t flinch.

- Work as part of a small, tight People team: everyone picks things up, and so will you.

What we’re looking for

- Comfortable with numbers. You can build a comp analysis in a spreadsheet and explain it to a manager who has never seen one.

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

title: Senior Applied ML Engineer | Kimchi (Model Router)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router 

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

- You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

- You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Containers
description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake. 

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

Who we are 

Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role, in a nutshell 

Chainguard Containers is our core product, and this team builds it. As a Staff Software Engineer in Container Product Engineering you will design and ship the features, services, and build systems behind Chainguard Containers, and you will lead the small sub-teams of two to four engineers that own them.

Chainguard is growing explosively. Every line of code is now written with AI in the loop, which means the foundation it runs on has to be secure by default. You will build that foundation: the hardened container images, the registry that serves them, and the tooling that lets engineers and AI agents adopt them.

This is a product role with technical ownership. You will set direction for major new capabilities, make the architectural calls that affect the team and the teams next to it, and multiply the output of the engineers around you. You will stay hands-on: most of your week is still building.

What the team owns 

- Product features for Chainguard Containers. Letting customers push their own images to our registry, Custom Assembly (customers compose images from our hardened packages), Helm charts, notifications, and compliance views such as STIG dashboards (STIG is the US government's hardening standard).

- The image build pipeline. The systems that turn packages from Wolfi, our Linux distribution, into signed and attested container images at scale, including moving image builds onto our own runner infrastructure.

- Registry performance and distribution. Work such as lazy loading, so a container starts before its whole image has downloaded, and image signing with Sigstore.

- Adoption tooling for engineers and AI agents. Migration tools that convert existing Dockerfiles to Chainguard Containers, and MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets AI agents call tools) so agents can discover and pull our images directly.

What you'll do 

- Architect and drive the delivery of major new features and services for Chainguard Containers, often spanning several engineers or teams, from concept through production and the first weeks of customer use.

- Make and own the high-leverage trade-offs: which capability to build first, what to defer, when to re-platform and when not to. Write the decision down and bring dissenting engineers along.

- Work with AI coding agents as part of how you build, review, and operate, and set the standard for how the team uses them safely as volume grows.

- Follow a problem wherever it goes: into another team's service, a customer call, a support ticket, or go-to-market data, and work across team boundaries to get ahead of planning cycles.

- Mentor and level up other engineers through design review and pair work, and set the standard for how the team designs, builds, and ships.

- Partner with Product and engineering leadership on roadmap, bringing a technical point of view to what we build, not only how.

- Keep the systems you own healthy: observability, on-call, and the fixes that stop the same page from coming back.

- Write clearly and often. Design notes, decision records, and status updates are how a remote team moves fast together.

What we're looking for 

- 5+ years building and operating software that paying customers use, including leading at least one multi-engineer project end to end, preferably at a startup or a company in hyper-growth.

- High agency and urgency. You find a way, you do not wait to be unblocked, and you unblock others.

- Judgment on trade-offs at the system level. You have made calls that moved a roadmap, and you can show what you gave up and why.

- A systems thinker who designs for the whole path: build pipeline, registry, distribution, and the customer's runtime, and who sees second-order effects before they land.

- AI-native in how you build and lead. You use agentic coding tools daily and you have changed how a team works because of them.

- Comfortable with ambiguity. You can turn a half-defined product goal into a concrete technical plan, and pivot when priorities shift.

- Architectural depth in Go: you can design a Go service from scratch, not only contribute to one, plus strong API design, databases and caching, and cloud infrastructure on GCP or AWS.

- Deep knowledge of containers, container registries, the OCI image format (Open Container Initiative, the standard for container images and registries), and Kubernetes.

- A track record of mentoring engineers and raising technical practices across a team.

- Low ego. You do what you say and say what you do, and you communicate early when the news is bad.

- Excellent written English and experience working on a distributed, remote-first team.

Nice to haves 

- Software supply chain security background: SBOMs (software bill of materials), Sigstore signing, or SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts, a framework for build integrity).

- Familiarity with Chainguard's open-source tools: Wolfi, apko, and melange.

- Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code experience.

- Author of or maintainer of open-source projects.

- A non-traditional path into engineering. We value people who learned by building.

Location 

Remote. United States preferred; Also available to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or relocation for this role.

Explore Our Work 

Dive into the practical side of what we do at Chainguard. These resources provide a hands-on look at our processes and offer an opportunity for in-depth understanding of our product offerings and the technology behind them.

Chainguard Academy 

Base Salary Range

$205,000 — $231,000 USD 

About Us

We live and breathe our company values:

- We are customer obsessed — We focus on delivering solutions to our customers that create value and make their lives better.

- We have a bias for intentional action — We prioritize, plan, try things, and fail fast.

- We don't take ourselves too seriously (but we do serious work) — We are solving an important problem which takes focus, but we also like to enjoy the journey.

- We trust each other and assume good intentions — We're transparent with decisions to empower team members to make well informed decisions.

A few of the benefits we offer:

- Flexible & Remote-First Culture: Work remotely with team meetup opportunities, bi-annual destination summits, and a monthly stipend for coworking spaces, phone and internet costs.

- Our Approach to Equity: Receive stock options upon hire and promotion. Plus, you can participate in secondary offerings and have 10 years to exercise your options (yes, you read that correctly: 10 years!).

- 100% Covered Health Insurance: We cover 100% of your health, vision and dental insurance premiums for you and your dependents. Nothing comes out of your paycheck.

- ∞ Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need – to do our best work, we need to recharge and reset.

- 18 Weeks Paid Parental Leave: We offer 18 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents, with the option to use it all at once or throughout your child's first year.

If your experience is close but doesn't fulfill all requirements, please apply. We're building the best team in technology and are focused on hiring "Chainguardians" with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.

title: Senior Thermomechanical Analysis Engineer – Extreme Environments (all genders)
description:
Your Mission: 

As Senior Thermomechanical Analysis Engineer (all genders) you will join VÆRIDION’s Technology division within the Mechanical Design & Integration team and lead the structural, stress, and thermomechanical finite element analysis (FEA) of the propulsion battery system for VÆRIDION’s CS-23 all-electric aircraft.

You will own the computational modelling of battery packs, power distribution units (PDUs), and their internal hardware, predicting how every component behaves under nominal and emergency conditions – including thermal runaway, the DO-160 environmental qualification conditions applied to the pack and PDU as airborne equipment (temperature and altitude, temperature variation, humidity, operational shocks and crash safety, and vibration), flight loads, and durability over service life. Your analysis will provide engineering evidence that the propulsion battery system is structurally robust, thermally safe, and certifiable.

Within the Mechanical Design & Integration team, you will collaborate with Mechanical Design, Materials & Processes, Test, HV Electrical Systems, Airborne Electronics, Thermal Systems, Aircraft Structures, Certification, Safety, and Quality teams to define analysis methods, apply the material property allowable required for your analyses, and substantiate the qualification of the propulsion battery pack and PDU. You will be the structural and thermomechanical analysis authority for the propulsion battery system, responsible for checking and releasing design against the applicable stress and thermomechanical requirements.

Your work will directly contribute to the propulsion battery system that underpins VÆRIDION’s mission to bring electric flight to regional aviation.

Your Day-to-Day: 

- Lead the structural, stress, and thermomechanical FEA of propulsion battery packs, PDUs, and their internal components, predicting how they behave under nominal operation and emergency conditions – including thermal runaway, the DO-160 environmental qualification conditions, and flight and inertial loads.

- Perform room-temperature and elevated-temperature analysis of composites (including sandwich structures), metals, adhesives, and mechanical fasteners, capturing temperature-dependent material behaviour.

- Build and correlate nonlinear models covering material, geometric, and contact nonlinearity – including cohesive-zone and VCCT delamination, composite progressive failure and damage propagation, metal plasticity and rate-dependent behaviour, crushable foam plasticity and densification, large-deformation and post-buckling response, and frictional contact with bolt pretension, including bearing behaviour at fastener holes (bearing yield, hole elongation, and bearing–bypass interaction).

- Model the hyper-elastic and viscoelastic behaviour of potting compounds, gap fillers, foams, gaskets, seals, and thermal interface materials to predict contact pressure and interface integrity across the life of the pack.

- Perform durability and life analysis across the differing service lives of components within the system, covering vibration-induced high-cycle fatigue (DO-160 random and sine sweep), low-cycle fatigue from ground–air–ground and charge/discharge thermal cycling, and fatigue of bonded joints, fasteners, busbars, and interconnects.

- Assess creep and stress relaxation of seals, adhesives, polymers, potting compounds, and thermal interface materials at elevated temperature, including loss of contact pressure across a pack replacement interval.

- Analyse thermal runaway response as a coupled thermomechanical event – pressure loads, direct impingement flow, ejecta, and heat transfer to surrounding structure and systems – working closely with the Thermal Systems team on thermal runaway CFD modelling and the resulting heat transfer boundary conditions, in support of containment and continued safe flight and landing.

- Apply static, fatigue, and creep material property allowable (room and elevated temperature) in the substantiation of the propulsion battery pack and PDU, working to established methodologies such as CMH-17 for composites and MMPDS for metallics, and specify the allowable, material data, and test conditions required from the Materials & Processes and Test teams.

- Automate and script analysis workflows – model generation, parametric studies, load case sweeps, and post-processing – using Python for Abaqus scripting, and develop closed-form and lower-order analysis methods in Python or MATLAB to size hardware quickly and to verify finite element results.

- Interface closely with the Mechanical Design, Materials & Processes, and Airborne Electronics teams to translate analysis results into design improvements and robust, certifiable hardware.

- Check and release design against the applicable stress and thermomechanical requirements, providing the stress sign-off for propulsion battery pack and PDU hardware releases.

- Define modelling standards, assumptions, load cases, and acceptance criteria, and maintain configuration-controlled analysis models and inputs.

- Support test planning and post-test correlation of FEA models against coupon, component, and full-scale test data.

- Author and release certification documentation, including analysis reports and means-of-compliance evidence for structural, environmental, and thermal runaway requirements.

Your Profile: 

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Structural/Computational Mechanics, or a related field; a PhD in a relevant area is beneficial.

- 5+ years of experience in structural/stress and thermomechanical FEA, preferably in aerospace, automotive, battery systems, or other high-performance engineering environments.

- Experience taking analytical responsibility for hardware, including checking the work of others and providing stress sign-off or equivalent release approval within a configuration-controlled environment, is desirable.

- Strong command of nonlinear FEA across material, geometric, and contact nonlinearity, with depth in several of the following: cohesive-zone modeling with traction–separation, composite progressive failure (e.g., Hashin/Puck), metal plasticity and viscoplasticity, hyperelastic and viscoelastic materials, crushable foam plasticity, large-deformation and buckling, and frictional contact with pretension, including fastener bearing and bearing–bypass analysis.

- Experience with room-temperature and elevated-temperature modeling of composites (including sandwich structures), metals, adhesives, and mechanical fasteners, covering temperature-dependent material behavior.

- Experience in fatigue and damage-tolerance analysis (S–N/ε–N methods, cumulative damage, random-vibration/PSD fatigue) and in creep and stress-relaxation behavior of adhesives and polymers at elevated temperature.

- Experience with explicit dynamics and impact/blast-type events (e.g., burst-disk actuation, vent impingement, ejecta and debris containment) is desirable.

- Proficiency with FEA software, ideally Abaqus; experience with tools such as Ansys (Mechanical/LS-DYNA), MSC/NX Nastran, Altair (HyperMesh/OptiStruct/Radioss), or COMSOL is beneficial.

- Experience implementing user-defined material models and subroutines in Abaqus (UMAT/VUMAT/UMATHT), including the ability to write and debug Fortran, is desirable.

- Proficiency in scripting: Python for Abaqus automation and post-processing, and Python or MATLAB for closed-form and lower-order analysis methods used to size hardware and verify finite element results.

- Proficiency with 3D CAD, ideally SolidWorks or CATIA, is desirable; experience with Siemens NX is beneficial.

- Experience applying static, fatigue, and creep material property allowables to the substantiation of structural hardware, including familiarity with CMH-17 and MMPDS methodologies or equivalent, and with A-/B-basis statistical allowables.

- Familiarity with aerospace environmental and structural requirements, in particular DO-160 environmental conditions and CS-23 structural substantiation, is desirable.

- Working knowledge of propulsion battery thermal runaway means of compliance, including DO-311A and the ANAC–EASA–FAA–TCCA harmonized thermal runaway white paper for propulsion batteries, is beneficial.

- Familiarity with development assurance and safety processes (e.g., ARP4754A/B, ARP4761/4761A, and ASTM F3230 for small aircraft) is beneficial.

- Experience with battery systems or electric propulsion systems is beneficial.

- Strong problem-solving skills, technical curiosity, and attention to detail.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary engineering environment.

- Fluent English language skills are essential; German language skills are beneficial.

Backed by some of the world’s leading venture capital firms, we’re on an ambitious mission to simplify and modernize every function of the dental practice through technology. As we expand our reach globally, Dandy is building the operating system for dental offices around the world—empowering clinicians and their teams with technology, innovation, and world-class support to achieve more for their practices, their people, and their patients.

About the Role: 

We’re looking for a highly consultative Dental Field Trainer in Germany to lead impactful, in-person training that accelerates early clinical success with Dandy’s digital dentistry solutions. This role is field-based, with up to 80% travel , and is focused on helping dental practices adopt intraoral scanning and digital workflows with confidence.

You’ll serve as a trusted clinical advisor to dentists, practice managers, and operational leaders—helping teams adopt new technology, digital workflows, improve clinical performance, and accelerate early success. This role combines clinical training expertise with operational execution and post-training insight to deliver measurable value at the intersection of training, technology, and practice growth. Success in this role comes from your ability to earn clinical trust and turn that trust into action — helping practices move from curiosity to confidence.

What You’ll Do: 

Training Delivery & Clinical Coaching 

- Lead high-touch, in-person trainings to support dentists and staff in adopting intraoral scanning and digital workflows.

- Coach teams based on live observation, reinforcing best practices and adapting in real time to meet the practice’s goals and maturity level.

- Take ownership of each practice’s success, driving early case submission by removing blockers, reinforcing clinical urgency, and building confidence during and immediately after training.

Clinical Advisory & Post-Training Analysis 

- Partner with clinicians and practice leaders to reinforce scanning habits and support early adoption.

- Monitor outcomes in the first 30 days and surface targeted coaching opportunities to accelerate success.

- Share field insights to inform scalable resources, improve onboarding, and strengthen future trainings.

Practice Readiness & Operational Alignment 

- Assess readiness across clinical workflows, team structure, and equipment to proactively surface blockers or risks.

- Coordinate with internal teams to ensure the right resources, messaging, and tools are in place before training day.

- Customize training strategies based on practice size, complexity, and clinical goals.

What We’re Looking For: 

- Clinical Training Experience: 3+ years of experience delivering clinical training in digital dentistry or dental technology, with strong familiarity with intraoral scanning and digital workflows.

- Clinical Advisor : Skilled at earning confidence from clinicians and staff by connecting clinical value to real-world outcomes

- Travel Readiness: Willingness and enthusiasm to travel up to 80% to deliver in-practice training and support.

- Proximity to Travel Hubs: Located near a major airport or transport hub.

- Leadership Presence: Comfortable partnering with senior leaders, clinicians, and staff across roles to influence behavior and drive adoption.

- In-Person Agility : Comfortable operating independently in the field, adjusting plans in real-time based on practice dynamics and needs.

- Strong Communicator: Excellent presentation and facilitation skills, with the ability to adjust tone and approach based on audience—whether working with hygienists or C-suite stakeholders.

- Native or near-native fluency in the local market language, with strong knowledge of local dental norms and terminology. English fluency is also required for global collaboration.

Customer-Centric Mindset: Passion for helping practices succeed, with a solutions-oriented approach to onboarding, training, and adoption.

title: Working Student Robotics Hardware & Electronics (m/f/d)
description:
Batch Robotics is revolutionizing how robots operate in factories — not through rigid programming or teaching by human demonstration, but with smart perception and AI intelligence. We are a team of 4 motivated people with +25 years of experience in industry and robotics. Our mission is to make robots smarter and more flexible, enabling batch-size-1 automation for surface treatment economically.

We are now looking for a Working Student / Werkstudent (m/f/d) to get hands-on with our robot systems. You will build, wire, and see hardware run in a real factory, working directly with our engineers and founders in our Munich lab.

Tasks

- Build & Wire: Assemble our robot cells — mount cobots, cameras and sensors, wire control cabinets, crimp cables, solder, and get the system powered up and running.

- Electronics & Measurement: Read and extend electrical schematics, select components, and debug with multimeter and oscilloscope until the signal is where it should be.

- Test & Script: Run bring-up and end-of-line tests, document what fails, and write small Python tools to talk to sensors, log data and automate repetitive steps.

- Prototype & Supply: Design and 3D-print mounts and adapters (we will teach you the CAD work), order components, and keep our lab and hardware stock in shape.

Requirements

- Studies: Enrolled in Electrical Engineering / Elektrotechnik, Mechatronics, Robotics or a related field at a Munich university — and staying enrolled for at least 6 more months.

- Hands-On by Nature: You build things outside of lectures — Formula Student, rocketry, a makerspace, RC models, a self-built PCB. You have actually held a soldering iron and a multimeter.

- Electrical Fundamentals: Comfortable with schematics, wiring and basic measurement gear. 24 V industrial wiring, control cabinets or fieldbuses are a plus, not a requirement.

- Programming Skills: You know your way around Linux and can write a Python script.

- Driver’s License: Class B — you occasionally pick up components at suppliers and join us for on-site work at customers.

- Availability & Mindset: ~20 h/week during the semester, ideally in full days, flexible in the breaks, on-site in Munich. Curious, reliable, and not scared by a system that does not work yet.

Benefits

- Real Hardware, Real Factories: You work on the systems we ship to customers, not on a training project — and you can join us on a deployment to see them run on a factory floor.

- Learn from Experts: Direct mentoring from founders and engineers with +25 years in industry and robotics — short feedback loops, no layers in between.

- Ownership & Path Forward: Your own topics from day one, a natural route into a Bachelor’s or Master’s thesis, and — if it fits both sides — a permanent role after your studies.

- Environment & Pay: A modern, central workspace in Munich, a well-equipped lab, an international team (working language English), and €16–18/h depending on experience.

Want to shape the future of industrial robotics? Send us your CV — a cover letter is not required. Tell us in two sentences what you have built with your own hands. We reply quickly and the process is short: a 20-minute intro call, then a visit to our lab in Munich so you can see the systems and meet the team.

title: Customer Support Manager (w/m/d) | GovTech Startup mit Impact
description:
Gestalte die Zukunft der öffentlichen Verwaltung mit uns! 

Ayunis (ehem. Locaboo) ist ein führendes GovTech-Startup aus München mit über 900 Kunden (Städte, Gemeinden, Kommunen) in der DACH-Region.

Aber öffentlicher Sektor? Ist das nicht super-bürokratisch? 

Das dachten wir zu Beginn auch. Doch der Sektor befindet sich stark im Wandel und du wirst bereits nach deinen ersten Gesprächen mit Kundinnen & Kunden merken, wie unglaublich offen und motiviert die Verwaltungsmitarbeitenden sind. Die Menschen dort sind einfach nur mega happy, dass sich bei der Digitalisierung endlich etwas tut.

Deine Rolle 

Als Customer Support Manager:in für Locaboo bist du Teil des Account-Management-Teams und die erste Anlaufstelle für unsere mehr als 900 Bestandskunden in der DACH-Region. Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Kundinnen & Kunden aus der öffentlichen Verwaltung schnell, kompetent und freundlich weiterkommen – ob per Ticket, Telefon oder im persönlichen Support-Call.

Aber du bist mehr als nur ein Helpdesk: Du gestaltest aktiv unsere Wissensbasis mit, entwickelst Inhalte für die Locaboo Academy und trägst so dazu bei, dass unsere Kundinnen & Kunden die Software langfristig erfolgreich nutzen. Als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Kundinnen & Kunden, Account Management und Produkt bringst du wertvolles Feedback aus dem Alltag direkt ins Team.

Das sagt deine Kollegin 

"Fast vier Monate bin ich inzwischen bei Ayunis, aber es fühlt sich an, als wäre ich schon viel länger Teil des Teams. Meine neuen Kolleg*innen haben es mir leicht gemacht, anzukommen. Die lockere Atmosphäre und die offene Kultur schätze ich sehr. 
Die Zusammenarbeit mit Kund*innen aus dem öffentlichen Sektor war für mich Neuland. Umso spannender ist es, in diese Welt einzutauchen. Ich habe in der kurzen Zeit unglaublich viel gelernt: über GovTech, über KI, über Locaboo und sogar über mich selbst. Genau diese Mischung aus neuen Herausforderungen und einem Team, in dem ich mich wohl fühle und auf das ich mich verlassen kann, macht die Arbeit hier für mich besonders." 

Sarah Unholzer – Account Managerin

Aufgaben 

- Du bearbeitest eingehende Support-Tickets unserer Bestandskundinnen & -kunden strukturiert und lösungsorientiert, sodass keine Anfrage verloren geht.

- Du bist erste Ansprechperson am Telefon und begleitest unsere Kundinnen & Kunden in Support-Calls durch ihre Anliegen.

- Du unterstützt Verwaltungsmitarbeitende im Rahmen von Support-Calls zu den Funktionen und Möglichkeiten von Locaboo und hilfst ihnen, die Software optimal einzusetzen.

- Du erstellst und pflegst Inhalte für unsere Locaboo Academy, von How-to-Artikeln über Video-Tutorials bis hin zu FAQ-Seiten, und bringst aktiv Ideen zur Weiterentwicklung ein.

- Du dokumentierst wiederkehrende Probleme und Kundenfeedback zu Locaboo und arbeitest eng mit dem Account Management Team und dem Produktteam zusammen, um nachhaltige Lösungen zu entwickeln.

- Du hast ein Gespür für Kundenpotenziale : Wenn du im Gespräch Upselling-Möglichkeiten erkennst, gibst du diese gezielt an das Account Management Team weiter.

- Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit dem Account Management Team neue Prozesse und Best Practices, um unseren Support kontinuierlich zu verbessern.

- Du denkst Support skalierbar: Du erkennst, wo sich Prozesse automatisieren lassen, und setzt das eigenständig um, z.B. mit Zendesk-Automatisierungen, KI Tools oder smarten Workflows.

Qualifikation 

- Du hast 2–3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Customer Support oder einer vergleichbaren Rolle – idealerweise in einem SaaS-Unternehmen oder (Gov)Tech-Umfeld.

- Du kennst dich im SaaS-Support aus und weißt, wie man Kundinnen & Kunden empathisch, klar und effizient durch technische Themen führt.

- Du bist kommunikationsstark , bleibst auch in stressigen Situationen freundlich und lösungsorientiert – am Telefon genauso wie im Ticket.

- Du arbeitest strukturiert, zuverlässig u nd verlierst auch bei vielen parallelen Anfragen nie den Überblick.

- Du bringst technische Affinität mit und hast Spaß daran, Software in- und auswendig zu kennen.

- Du verfügst über verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und hast Englischkenntnisse auf C1/C2 Niveau.

- Plus-Punkte:

- Du hast bereits mit Zendesk gearbeitet und kennst dich mit Ticket-Workflows aus

- Du hast Erfahrung mit StartDeliver, HubSpot oder einem ähnlichen CRM-Tool.

- Du hast Erfahrung in der Erstellung von Help-Center-Inhalten, Tutorials oder ähnlichem Content.

Benefits 

- 💸 55.000–60.000€ Jahresgehalt

- 🎓 2.000€ Entwicklungsbudget pro Jahr zur freien Verfügung

- 🏝️ 30 Urlaubstage

- 🏋 Zugang zu über 10.000 Fitnesstudios & Sportangeboten mit dem EGYM Wellpass

- 🚅 Bezuschussung des Deutschlandtickets oder Tankgutschein

- 📈 Du hast die Möglichkeit, in einem schnell wachsenden Startup mit 25+ Mitarbeitenden von Beginn an dabei zu sein und dieses aktiv mitzugestalten

- 📍 Unbefristeter Arbeitsvertrag, flexible Arbeitszeiten & hybrides Arbeiten sowie Workation im EU-Ausland

- 🛖 Neues Office in München mit voll ausgestatteter Küche, gemütlicher Lounge-Ecke und

- 🏊 einem 50 Meter langen Outdoor-Pool (!)

- 💻 Neueste technische Ausstattung (MacBook)

- 🎉 Regelmäßige Team-Events & Off-Sites

🤗 Kein perfektes Profil? Kein Problem! 

Wir wissen, dass niemand alles kann. Wenn du neugierig bist, Lust am Lernen hast und Dinge voranbringen möchtest, wollen wir dich kennenlernen.

Lass uns einfach wissen, wer du bist – Lebenslauf oder LinkedIn-Profil reicht. Kein Bewerbungsepos nötig .

⚡ Wir geben Gas. Genau wie du. 

Niemand wartet gerne. Deshalb haben wir unseren Bewerbungsprozess so schlank wie möglich gehalten. Wir schätzen deine Zeit und melden uns nach deiner Bewerbung in der Regel innerhalb von 2-3 Werktagen bei dir zurück. Unser persönlicher Bestwert von der Bewerbung bis zum unterschriebenen Vertrag liegt bei 3 Tagen. Wir sind bereit, wenn du es bist. Lass uns also keine Zeit verlieren!

title: Senior Software Engineer Computer Vision (f/m/d)
description:
Agricultural Innovation at Organifarms

We are a startup at the forefront of agricultural innovation, specializing in the development of harvesting robots for strawberries. Our mission is to revolutionize the way strawberries are harvested, making it more efficient, sustainable, and cost-effective

You have...

- Completed degree in computer science with specialization in robotics, computer vision or a comparable field of study

- 3 years of hands-on experience with 2D/3D computer vision, machine learning and 3D vision sensors

- Profound skills with Python, PyTorch, OpenCV, Docker, Linux and Git

- Experience with ROS 2 (Robot Operating System) in production

- A passion for the development of innovative solutions and creative ideas to improve our robots

- Team spirit and entrepreneurial thinking

- Fluency in English is required, fluency in German is a big plus

Your role at Organifarms:

- You will develop computer vision pipelines for 7-axis robots used for harvesting. Our robot operates in a greenhouse and faces a highly dynamic environment. Changing light conditions, fast robot movements and movable targets are challenges the vision system has to overcome.

- You will rapidly prototype your designs and ideas on real hardware

Depending on your skills and interests:

- Developing algorithms for panoptic segmentation of the robot's environment

- Developing self-learning vision-based robot control algorithms

- Developing 3D object detection, e.g., generation of collision objects using 3D perception sensors (LiDAR, stereo cameras) and their respective point clouds

- Integrating new vision sensors to enhance the robot’s understanding of the environment

- Developing vision-based tracking methods

Benefits at Organifarms:

- 30 days of vacation

- Hansefit membership or Givve Card

- Flexible working hours

- Free beverages and fruits

- Homeoffice

- Motivated and talented team with a passion for innovative ideas

Your application

If you match most of these requirements and want to help shape the future of agricultural robotics, we encourage you to apply.

title: Cloud Platform Engineer – Connected Medical Devices
description:
About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Cloud Platform Engineer to build and operate the cloud services layer behind our connected medical device platform on Microsoft Azure — from device telemetry ingress through storage, orchestration, and clinical system integration, under HIPAA and GDPR constraints.

Key Responsibilities

- Design and operate the REST/HTTPS device-to-cloud ingestion path (TLS 1.2/1.3, mTLS or token-based device auth) and manage the device certificate lifecycle
- Implement tiered storage and data pipelines across Data Lake Gen2, Cosmos DB, Azure SQL, and Data Factory / Stream Analytics, with US–EU data residency separation
- Enforce platform security: encryption, Key Vault, Entra ID access control, Private Link isolation, audit logging, and secure SDLC
- Translate HIPAA and GDPR obligations into concrete Azure controls and continuous compliance evidence; align with IEC 62304 and ISO 13485 where applicable
- Integrate clinical systems via Azure Health Data Services (FHIR R4, DICOM, HL7v2) and SMART on FHIR authorization
- Build licensing and entitlement services, and integrate payment providers (Stripe, Adyen) with reliable webhook and billing lifecycle handling
- Operate multi-tenant device fleet and user management, including device twins, configuration distribution, and role-based access for clinicians and patients
- Deliver signed OTA updates via Azure Device Update, with staged rollout, rollback, and a full audit trail
- Own Azure infrastructure as code (Bicep/Terraform), CI/CD, observability, cost management, and DR/BCP
Required Qualifications

- 6+ years in cloud engineering, including 3+ years hands-on Azure in production
- Strong Node.js and TypeScript development experience for backend services and APIs, plus Python for data tooling
- Production experience with high-throughput REST/HTTPS APIs, TLS/mTLS, and certificate-based client authentication
- Demonstrated device-to-cloud IoT architecture at fleet scale
- Working knowledge of HIPAA and GDPR as engineering requirements, not just policy
- Infrastructure-as-code, CI/CD, and observability as everyday practice
Preferred Qualifications

- Azure Authentication, Azure Data Storage, Azure Health Data Services / FHIR experience
- Background in regulated industries (medical devices, aerospace, automotive) — IEC 62304, ISO 13485, EU MDR
- Multi-region, multi-tenant SaaS with data residency constraints
- Azure certifications (AZ-305, AZ-500, AZ-220);
What We Offer

Work with direct impact on patient outcomes, a technically broad role across IoT and cloud, a quality-driven engineering culture, and competitive compensation and development support.

title: Masseur / Physiotherapeuth (m/w/d) - Deimann Spa
description:
Wenn ein Gast nach einer Behandlung tiefenentspannt den Deimann Spa verlässt, ist genau das der Moment, in dem Ihre Arbeit spürbar wird. Mit fachlichem Können, Ruhe und einem sicheren Gespür für die individuellen Bedürfnisse unserer Gäste machen Sie aus einer Massage oder Wellnessanwendung eine wertvolle Auszeit.

Im Deimann Spa, dem Wellnessbereich unseres 5-Sterne-Superior-Hotels im Sauerland, verbinden wir professionelle Anwendungen mit herzlicher persönlicher Betreuung. Sie arbeiten in einem hochwertigen Umfeld, in dem Qualität nicht nur bei der Behandlung zählt, sondern auch in jedem Kontakt mit unseren Gästen.

Aufgaben

- Führen Sie klassische und wellnessorientierte Massageanwendungen professionell und mit einem sicheren Gespür für die individuellen Bedürfnisse unserer Gäste durch.

- Setzen Sie Ihr fachliches Wissen bei physiotherapeutischen Anwendungen ein, sofern diese Ihrer Qualifikation entsprechen, und begleiten Sie unsere Gäste verantwortungsvoll auf ihrem Weg zu mehr Wohlbefinden.

- Beraten Sie unsere Gäste individuell zu passenden Massage- und Wellnessanwendungen und finden Sie gemeinsam mit ihnen die Behandlung, die zu ihren persönlichen Bedürfnissen passt.

- Erkennen Sie im Rahmen Ihrer fachlichen Qualifikation die individuellen Bedürfnisse unserer Gäste und stimmen Sie Ihre Behandlung entsprechend darauf ab.

- Betreuen Sie unsere Gäste während ihres gesamten Aufenthalts im Deimann Spa aufmerksam, herzlich und professionell.

- Bereiten Sie die Behandlungsräume sorgfältig vor und nach, damit jede Anwendung in einer ruhigen, gepflegten und hochwertigen Atmosphäre stattfinden kann.

- Sichern Sie durch Ihre sorgfältige Arbeitsweise die hohen Hygiene- und Qualitätsstandards unseres Spa-Bereichs.

- Arbeiten Sie eng mit Ihrem Spa-Team zusammen und tragen Sie dazu bei, dass unsere Gäste fachlich kompetent und persönlich aufmerksam betreut werden.

- Gestalten Sie mit Ihrer Arbeit ein Spa-Erlebnis, das unseren Gästen Ruhe, Entspannung und die besondere Qualität des Hotel Deimann vermittelt.

- Arbeiten Sie überwiegend tagsüber bis in die Abendstunden, regulär bis etwa 19:00 Uhr. Auch Sonn- und Feiertage gehören zu Ihrem Arbeitsalltag.

Qualifikation

- Sie verfügen über eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Masseur/in, Physiotherapeut/in oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation, damit Sie unsere Gäste fachlich kompetent und verantwortungsvoll behandeln können.

- Sie bringen idealerweise praktische Erfahrung in Massage, Physiotherapie, Wellness oder einem Spa mit – aber auch als Berufseinsteiger/in sind Sie willkommen, wenn Ihre fachliche Qualifikation und Ihre Haltung zu uns passen.

- Sie verfügen über fachliche Kompetenz und arbeiten sorgfältig, weil hochwertige Massage- und Wellnessanwendungen ein hohes Maß an Verantwortung und Präzision erfordern.

- Sie haben Freude am direkten Kontakt mit Menschen, weil eine gute Spa-Behandlung nicht nur von der richtigen Technik, sondern ebenso von Aufmerksamkeit und Einfühlungsvermögen lebt.

- Sie arbeiten serviceorientiert und aufmerksam, damit sich unsere Gäste während ihrer gesamten Behandlung persönlich wahrgenommen und bestens aufgehoben fühlen.

- Sie treten gepflegt und professionell auf, weil Ihr persönliches Auftreten wesentlich zur hochwertigen Atmosphäre im Deimann Spa beiträgt.

- Sie arbeiten selbstständig, zuverlässig und verantwortungsbewusst, damit sich unsere Gäste jederzeit auf Ihre fachliche und persönliche Betreuung verlassen können.

- Sie sind ein Teamplayer und unterstützen Ihre Kolleginnen und Kollegen, weil ein außergewöhnliches Spa-Erlebnis nur gemeinsam entstehen kann.

- Sie bringen Flexibilität und Bereitschaft zur Arbeit an Sonn- und Feiertagen mit, da unser Spa auch an diesen Tagen für unsere Gäste geöffnet ist.
