title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

What’s in it for you?

title: Senior Applied ML Engineer | Kimchi (Model Router)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router 

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've spent 5+ years in applied ML or ML research, and you've trained, evaluated, and shipped models that make real-time decisions (ranking, recommendation, bandits, pricing, or LLM routing) and you can tell that story with receipts.

- Strong Python and SQL at scale: you can pull, clean, and interrogate millions of request-level records without waiting on anyone.

- You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

- You have real opinions about what LLM benchmarks measure, agentic harnesses included.

- You know enough serving reality (TTFT, decode speed, batching, prefix caching, concurrency) to model the objective honestly.

- You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Own the routing model end to end: features, objective, training, calibration, and release cadence. Iterate it like a product, not a research artifact.

- Build the evaluation that gates every change: production-parity benchmarks, router-vs-router comparisons, holdouts by task family, error bars on pass rates.
Nothing ships on vibes.

- Turn fleet data into training signal: per-request outcomes from production, benchmark rollouts, and override feedback, with failure categorization (infra vs
task) so poisoned labels never reach the policy.

- Model the objective the user actually experiences: task success × token cost × wall-clock speed under the real concurrency regime, with cached-input
economics in the picture.

- Run the online loop: shadow, A/B, full rollout, drift monitoring, retrain. When production disagrees with your offline eval, you find out why before the next
ship.

- Push the frontier where it pays: calibrated decisions, abstention under uncertainty, speed-aware routing. We experiment on what a router should be, not just
which model it picks today.

- Partner with platform engineers on instrumentation: the features and labels recorded per request (decode speed first-class among them) and the experiments
the data path must support.

title: Social Media & Project Coordination (m/f/d), Fashion Week Focus
description:
About us 
Fashion Revolution Germany e.V. is the German chapter of Fashion Revolution, the global movement for a clean, safe, fair, transparent and accountable fashion industry. Since the Rana Plaza factory collapse in 2013, the movement has asked one question: Who made my clothes? As a non-profit association of designers, educators, communicators and activists, we run campaigns, workshops and events that make fashion’s social and environmental impacts visible and show practical alternatives such as repair, upcycling and circular models.

The project: RE/CLAIMED at Berlin Fashion Week 
A key focus of this internship is RE/CLAIMED, a multidisciplinary sustainable fashion show supported by Fashion Revolution Germany. RE/CLAIMED combines upcycled runway looks, dance, live performance, music and interactive installations to change how people value their clothes. After a sold-out first edition in January 2026, the second edition will take place with around 400 guests expected.

Your role 
You’ll pilot the day-to-day social media activities for RE/CLAIMED in the run-up to Berlin Fashion Week, during the show and in the follow-up. You’ll also support the coordination of the show and of Fashion Revolution Germany’s projects in Berlin. You’ll work directly with Eric Vincent Vinsonneau, who leads RE/CLAIMED, and alongside our communications partners.

Beyond RE/CLAIMED, you’ll take part in other Fashion Revolution Germany activities in Berlin. One example is our stand at the Alt-Rixdorfer Christmas Market in Neukölln on the weekend of 4–6 December 2026, where you’ll help with preparation, on-site support and social media coverage.

Your tasks 

Social media (main focus) 

- Plan and manage the content calendar for RE/CLAIMED’s Instagram, and optionally build a TikTok presence

- Create posts, stories and reels: behind the scenes, designer and performer portraits, countdowns and impact facts

- Cover the show live and produce recap content afterwards

- Engage with the community, partners, designers and press, and track performance

Project coordination 

- Support show preparation: partners, designers, models, dancers, volunteers and schedules

- Help with on-site logistics on the show day

- Support other Fashion Revolution Germany projects in Berlin as needed

Your profile 

- You have a strong interest in sustainable fashion and social or environmental topics

- You have experience creating social media content, ideally including short-form video

- You have a good eye for aesthetics and storytelling

- You’re organised, reliable and proactive, and comfortable working independently in a small team

- You speak fluent English (our working language). German is a strong plus.

- Bonus: Canva, CapCut, Adobe or similar tools; experience with events, fashion or non-profits

- Use data, feedback, research and production issues to improve product decisions.

- Launch features, monitor performance and drive iterations.

- Experience as Product Manager, Product Owner, founder, growth/product operator or similar role.

- Strong product sense and ability to simplify complex workflows.

- Able to work with engineers and designers to ship real products.

- Comfortable with metrics, user feedback, experiments and post-launch learning.

- Strong writing, prioritization and stakeholder management.

- High ownership and ability to drive work with limited guidance.

- Starts from user problems, not feature lists.

- Can make decisions with incomplete information.

title: iOS Software Engineer
description:
About ActAI 

There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting.

Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. We believe products will greatly reduce hallucinations.

Our objective is to organise anyone's life, allowing us all to spend time on valuable and meaningful things.

Role

As an iOS Software Engineer, you own the iOS client experience, how AI feels, responds, and performs in users’ hands. This is not a thin integration role. You will build a production-grade iOS application where AI interactions are central to product experience, and performance, reliability, and user trust are critical.

Focus 

- Build and maintain iOS applications using Swift and SwiftUI.

- Integrate AI-powered features through backend APIs.

- Design UX patterns for AI interactions, including loading states, streaming responses, retries, and fallbacks.

- Optimize performance, memory usage, and battery efficiency.

- Capture user signals and feedback to support AI evaluation and iteration.

- Collaborate closely with backend and ML engineers on API design and system behavior.

- Maintain high App Store quality, stability, and production reliability.

Ideal Experiences 

- 3+ years of iOS development experience using Swift.

- Hands-on experience integrating AI-powered features into mobile apps.

- Strong understanding of async/await, concurrency, and background tasks.

- Solid iOS performance and memory optimization skills.

- Experience shipping and maintaining production iOS apps.

- Comfort designing for latency, partial failure, and non-deterministic AI behavior.

- Exposure to CoreML or light on-device ML.

- Familiarity with feature flags or remote configuration systems.

- Strong intuition for AI UX patterns and user trust considerations.

Outcomes 

- Stable, smooth, and reliable real-world use iOS applications.

- Performance is optimized: responsive, low-latency, and efficient on memory and CPU.

- Production issues are detected early, monitored effectively, and resolved with clear root-cause analysis.

Tech Stack 

- Swift

- SPM

- SwiftUI

- SQL / noSQL

- TensorFlow Lite (on-device inference)

How We Work 

The best products today in the world were built by small, world class teams. We are a high talent density and hands-on team. We make decisions collectively, move at rapid speed, striking a balance between shipping high quality work and learning. Joining our team requires the ability to bring structure, exercise judgment, and execute independently. Our goal is to put in hands of our users a truly magical product

Applications are evaluated by our technical team members. Interviews will be conducted via virtual meetings and/or onsite.

This isn't just a job offer; it's an invitation to be part of a team that's bringing AI to have practical benefits to billions globally.

title: Employee Experience and People Analytics Lead
description:
Castrol is one of the world’s leading lubricant brands, serving customers and consumers in the automotive, marine, industrial and energy sectors. Castrol brands are recognised globally for their premium quality and high performance, shaped by the company’s commitment to innovation and cutting-edge technology. Whether you're just starting out or ready for your next big move, you're in the right place to explore an exciting career with Castrol. 

Job description 

About the team

This is a unique opportunity to shape and lead Castrol’s employee listening and people analytics capability during a critical period of organisational transformation. As the Employee Experience & People Analytics Lead, you will act as the central expert and trusted advisor for employee listening across the business, partnering closely with senior leaders, HR Business Partners, Centres of Expertise, and transformation teams.

You will have ownership of Castrol’s employee listening platform and strategy, ensuring employee feedback is translated into meaningful action that improves engagement, culture, organisational effectiveness, and business performance. With approximately 6,300 employees across 40 countries, the role offers significant global exposure and the opportunity to influence decision-making at the highest levels.

This is a highly visible, business-facing role that goes beyond survey administration. Success will come from your ability to combine employee experience expertise, people analytics, stakeholder management, and data storytelling to help leaders make evidence-based decisions during a period of ongoing change.

Key tasks

- Lead Castrol's Employee Listening Capability

- Act as the primary point of contact for all employee listening and survey activity across the organisation.

- Own the implementation, configuration, governance, administration, and continuous improvement of the Qualtrics Employee Experience platform.

- Design and deliver a range of employee listening initiatives, including engagement surveys, pulse surveys, lifecycle surveys, moments that matter surveys, and transformation-related listening programmes.

- Develop and maintain an employee listening strategy that aligns with Castrol's transformation agenda and business objectives.

- Establish governance frameworks, survey standards, and reporting methodologies that ensure data privacy, consistency, and insight quality.

- Deliver actionable workforce insights

- Analyse employee experience, workforce, talent, and organisational data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and areas for intervention.

- Combine multiple data sources to provide leadership with a holistic view of organisational health and workforce effectiveness.

- Support workforce planning, organisational design, talent management, employee engagement, and retention initiatives through data-driven insights.

- Identify leading indicators and predictive insights that help anticipate workforce risks and opportunities.

- Influence decision-making through reporting and storytelling

- Create executive dashboards, leadership scorecards, PowerPoint presentations, and insight packs that translate data into compelling business narratives.

- Present findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders and leadership teams.

- Facilitate action-planning discussions and workshops that help leaders convert employee feedback into meaningful organisational outcomes.

- Act as a trusted advisor, providing evidence-based recommendations on employee experience and workforce challenges.

Experience needed

- We're looking for an experienced Employee Experience, People Analytics, or Organisational Effectiveness professional who combines deep technical expertise with strong consulting and stakeholder management skills.

- Significant hands-on experience with Qualtrics or similar survey software.

- Proven experience leading or playing a major role in a full Qualtrics implementation from the ground up.

- Approximately 5+ years of experience working with employee listening platforms, survey technology, and survey design.

- Experience building dashboards, managing enterprise reporting frameworks, and generating actionable business insights.

- Strong people analytics capability, with experience turning workforce and engagement data into compelling recommendations for senior stakeholders.

- Experience operating within large, complex organisations of 1,000+ employees, ideally in global environments.

- Demonstrable experience supporting employee listening programmes across multiple countries.

- Advanced Excel and PowerPoint skills, with the ability to analyse data and communicate findings effectively.

What will make you stand out:

- Experience supporting global employee populations and large-scale change or transformation programmes.

- Experience with alternative employee listening platforms such as Medallia, Peakon, Glint, InMoment, or similar technologies.

- Expertise in employee listening governance, data privacy, survey methodology, and enterprise-scale deployment.

- Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence senior leaders and drive action from insights.

- Experience creating executive dashboards, scorecards, and board-level reporting.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have deployed and operated enterprise-scale employee listening programmes rather than those whose experience is limited to academic or survey administration use cases. title: Staff Digital Marketing Manager
description:
What is Flagstone? 

Flagstone is many things. An online savings platform, reinventing how individuals, businesses, and charities manage, protect, and grow their cash. A diverse group of people, bound by a collaborative spirit, and shared purpose. And lastly, a thriving, profitable business – where smart people do their best work.

Each definition shares a common thread: our unique culture. It’s our pride and joy. And our competitive advantage.

A feel for our culture: 

To revolutionise the savings market, we need to be at our best. But high performance takes more than talent – it takes a culture of kindness, respect, and growth.

That’s why we’re building a diverse, inclusive community, where your voice is heard and valued. Where, with close support and room to develop, you can surpass even your own expectations. And be rewarded for it.

We may not change the world, but we can change the world of financial technology. And all it takes is a winning mix of drive, talent, and empathy. Our culture celebrates all three.

But enough about us. Let’s talk about you.

Does this sound like you? 

You’re a senior digital marketing leader who has owned strategy at scale, you’re as comfortable presenting to executives as you are getting hands-on with performance data. You know how to turn insight into clear commercial decisions and how to build and develop a high-performing team, and you have the credibility to keep digital front and centre in senior conversations. You’re also curious about how AI is changing search, and ready to grow your expertise as it evolves.

What you'll do 

You'll report to the Head of Digital and CRM and own our digital marketing strategy and implementation from end to end. As the senior strategic voice for digital, you'll turn data and market insight into a clear, commercially led strategy, and make sure every channel and partner delivers to a high standard. You'll also be the link between digital performance and the wider business, keeping digital front and centre in executive decision-making.

This will include:

- Owning digital marketing strategy and delivery across all channels, including AI and LLM search visibility, so our approach is joined up and commercial wherever Flagstone shows up

- Managing our agency and external partner relationships, including performance, commercial terms, and governance

- Shaping what we need from our marketing technology stack as the landscape evolves

- Using data and digital expertise to plan budgets, set channel strategy, and guide investment, turning performance insight into clear commercial outcomes

- Giving senior leaders clear, credible, and timely updates on digital performance and strategy

- Building and developing a high-performing digital team, with the capability, structure, and culture to make digital a key driver of Flagstone's long-term growth strategy

What you'll bring 

- Substantial experience in a senior digital marketing leadership role, with hands-on expertise across digital channels and agency management

- A track record of setting and delivering digital strategy at scale

- Strong commercial and data skills, with the ability to turn performance data into clear recommendations and sound investment decisions

- Confidence and credibility when presenting digital performance and strategy to senior leaders and executives

- Proven people leadership experience, with a track record of managing, developing, and growing high-performing teams

- Working knowledge of AI and large language model (LLM) search visibility, or the drive to build this expertise quickly as the landscape evolves

- Experience of thriving in a high-growth, ambitious business, with financial services experience helpful but not essential

How we reward you: 

At Flagstone, the benefits extend beyond false gifts like “fruit and snacks”. Instead, we invest in your health, wealth, and professional development. Here’s a selection of our benefits:

- Hybrid working - Spend at least 1 day a week with your team in our collaborative London office

- Competitive bonus scheme - designed to reward and recognise high performance

- Flexible benefits budget - a pot to fund meaningful benefits for you, whether it's hormone or fertility testing, cancer screening, neuro-diversity coaching or something that matters for you.

- A range of salary sacrifice options to help you make tax efficient savings on electric cars, nursery schemes, home and tech goods.

- Private health care - Enjoy all the benefits AXA has to offer, including reduced gym memberships and medical history disregarded

- 25 days holiday - plus bank holidays, well-being days and volunteering days

- Enhanced Parental Leave – enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption pay.

All are welcome. 

At Flagstone, we’re assembling a diverse team that defies our industry’s norms. Think this role could suit you? We encourage you to apply, no matter your background.

title: Senior Creative Designer
description:
At Brevo, we’re not just building a CRM. With our technology, we’re helping millions of organizations build lasting relationships with their customers. 

From emails and SMS to WhatsApp, Chat, and Marketing Automation, our tools are intuitive, powerful, and built to scale with every ambition. We give businesses a clear view of the customer journey, so they can focus on what matters: connection.

As a certified B Corp , we’re proud to grow with purpose, committed to high standards of social and environmental impact, not just performance.

Today, more than 500,000 businesses across 180 countries —from NGOs like Amnesty International to global brands like Carrefour, eBay, Louis Vuitton, and Michelin—trust Brevo to engage their audiences, cut through complexity, and deliver results. Our reliable technology and 75+ integrations help them create unparalleled customer experiences, without the usual tech headaches.

We recently exceeded 200m ARR and reached a major milestone by becoming a Unicorn , backed by strong growth and global expansion - and we’re just getting started!

The role 

We’re looking for a Senior Creative Designer to join our Brand team in Paris. You’ll help build a brand that is understood, remembered and trusted, making a powerful product feel simple, human and desirable. As part of our creative team, you’ll shape Brevo’s visual identity, content and digital presence across every channel and market. We believe great design starts with great thinking, so we question the brief, look for the sharpest idea and make sure it holds across every touchpoint.

Your impact at Brevo 

- Contribute to the evolution of Brevo's visual identity and brand guidelines, ensuring consistency across every touchpoint, from paid ads to event signage.

- Design marketing and communication assets for product launches and campaigns, adapting concepts across channels, formats and markets (digital, social media, OOH, events, print).

- Produce social-first content, including video, motion and short-form, for LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and X, tailored to each platform's codes.

- Build content plans that combine organic, paid and evergreen content, then measure performance and keep improving.

- Translate complex product features into simple, engaging messages for different audiences and markets.

- Partner with Growth, Product, Sales and Leadership to align creative work with business objectives.

- Experiment with new formats and AI-powered creative tools, and bring what works into the team's workflow.

Who you are 

- Around 6 years of experience in creative, brand or content design, ideally in an agency, startup or SaaS/tech company, with a strong portfolio of brand, content and digital work.

- You think before you design: you take the time to understand the product, challenge briefs constructively and turn complex ideas into clear visual stories.

- You have a solid understanding of B2B communication, paid campaigns, social media best practices and storytelling.

- You’re comfortable with AI creative tools (Midjourney, Runway, Kling, Claude…)

- You're fluent in Figma (mandatory, including design systems) Adobe suite.

- You're autonomous and organised, juggle several projects at once and take ownership from idea to execution.

- You communicate in professional English (C1 or above).

- Bonus points if you have B2C experience, speak French.

If you don't meet all the requirements above but believe this opportunity matches your expectations and experience, we still encourage you to apply! 

Why people love working at Brevo 

- A place to grow, together: Join an international team in a bright, collaborative office located in a vibrant neighborhood.

- Practical perks for everyday balance: RTT days off, 50% public transport reimbursement, Sustainable Mobility Package (whether you ride a classic bike or go electric, we support your choice to commute greener) and daily Swile meal vouchers (€12.50/day).

- Learning, every step of the way: Access to English classes and 155,000+ courses on Udemy, plus a strong internal culture of knowledge-sharing and support.

- Flexible for life: A remote-friendly setup, budget to support your home workspace, and relocation assistance for international talents.

- Wellbeing that works: Top-notch private healthcare (70% covered), 6-week second-parent leave, extra time off if your child is sick and needs you, and several services related to prevention, health and personal and professional well-being on Welii platform

- A culture that cares: From inter-office trips to regular team events, there are plenty of ways to connect beyond your day-to-day. You'll also find active social, green, and LGBTQIA+ communities, plus Work Council benefits via Leeto, all here to support what matters to you, inside and outside of work.

Our candidate journey 

- Introductory TA call (30 min)

- Meeting and Portfolio review with Rémi, Senior Brand & Com Director. (40 min)

- Creative case study (4–5 hours of work) and presentation (45 min)

- Final interview with our CMO (30 min)

- Reference check 

Whoever you are, wherever you’re from, if this role speaks to you, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Technical Support & Operations Engineer
description:
Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. 

Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions 

Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀 

About the Role 

As part of the continued growth of our activities and the deployment of our photonic Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) to international customers, we are looking for a Technical Support & Operations Technician / Engineer to join our team.

You will contribute to the operational monitoring of Quandela's QPUs and other hardware products deployed at customer sites , ensuring their proper operation and supporting maintenance activities, both remotely and on site.

Working at the interface between Quandela's technical teams and system users, you will develop a broad understanding of our products, particularly the interactions between hardware equipment and software control interfaces. You will perform initial technical investigations when issues arise and involve the relevant technical experts when required.

The role combines technical support, maintenance, field interventions, training and continuous improvement in a complex and international technological environment.

Internal training will provide you with the specific knowledge required to understand our technology and systems. No previous experience in quantum computing is required. 

As our support and maintenance activities are still being structured, you will also contribute to improving our processes, tools and operational methods.

Your Key Responsibilities: 

System operations & technical support 

You will contribute to maintaining the operational performance and availability of QPUs and other hardware products deployed at customer sites.

- Monitor the operation and performance of installed systems.
- Analyse operational data and identify anomalies or performance degradation.
- Perform initial technical investigations to characterise issues and help determine the appropriate resolution path.
- Follow up on technical incidents and corrective actions with the relevant teams.
- Maintain accurate technical records of systems and interventions.
- Provide remote technical support to customers and trained personnel working on the systems.

Maintenance & customer-site interventions 

You will contribute to the preparation and follow-up of preventive and corrective maintenance activities.

- Track maintenance schedules and anticipate upcoming interventions.
- Identify the resources, equipment, spare parts and technical expertise required for each intervention.
- Perform diagnostic, maintenance and system recovery operations according to established procedures.
- Support technicians and technical experts remotely or on site during interventions.
- Perform functional checks and testing following maintenance activities.
- Track completed actions, outstanding issues and upcoming maintenance requirements.
The role involves business travel within France and internationally , with frequency and duration depending on the needs of our installed systems. 

User training & technical guidance 

You will help customers and technical operators become increasingly autonomous in operating and maintaining our QPUs.

- Train users and technical operators on routine QPU operation and maintenance activities.
- Support users in operating the systems and their control interfaces.
- Share best practices for operation, troubleshooting and maintenance.
- Contribute to the creation and improvement of training materials and technical documentation.

Documentation & continuous improvement 

You will ensure the traceability of technical operations and contribute to structuring our support and maintenance activities.

- Prepare technical monitoring, intervention and maintenance reports.
- Maintain up-to-date technical documentation for installed systems.
- Contribute to writing and improving diagnostic, maintenance and operating procedures.
- Capitalise on field experience to improve reliability and facilitate future interventions.
- Contribute to implementing tools and methods for the structured monitoring of our installed systems.

Requirements 

Education & experience

- Associate's, Bachelor's or Master's degree in instrumentation, applied physics, optoelectronics or a related technical field.
- The position is open to both experienced technicians and engineers with a strong interest in hands-on, operational activities .
- Previous experience in operations, system integration, maintenance or technical support for complex systems is preferred.
- Experience working in a multidisciplinary hardware/software environment is highly valued.
- Experience supporting or maintaining technical equipment installed at customer sites would be an advantage.

Technical skills Required 

- Good understanding of complex technical systems combining hardware and software.
- Knowledge of electronics, instrumentation and/or control systems.
- Ability to analyse operational data and characterise technical issues.
- Ability to perform diagnostic and maintenance operations according to established procedures.
- Ability to identify and involve the appropriate technical experts when required.
- Strong organisational skills and ability to rigorously track interventions, deadlines and outstanding actions.
- Ability to follow, write and improve technical procedures.
- Professional fluency in English, both written and spoken , as you will interact directly with international customers and colleagues, deliver training sessions and produce technical documentation.
- Willingness and ability to travel internationally.
Nice to have

- Knowledge of optics, photonics and/or cryogenics .
- Hands-on experience with optical systems, including basic optical alignment.
- Experience operating or maintaining cryogenic systems.
- Basic programming or scripting skills, particularly Python .
- Experience maintaining scientific or industrial equipment.
- Experience delivering technical training to users or operators.
Benefits 

- Competitive salary, flexible based on your experience 
- Profit-sharing & company savings plan
- 100% health coverage (Alan)
- 50% transport reimbursement or sustainable mobility bonus
- Meal vouchers (Swile), Gymlib fitness support
- Childcare assistance & referral bonuses (€1,000–€2,000)

What we offer

- A meaningful role with real ownership, from day one
- A team eager to collaborate and grow with you
- A hybrid work model (3 days/week onsite in Massy, 1 day in Paris, 1 to 2 days remotely)
- Daily exposure to the entire quantum stack — from high-level APIs to low-level firmware, and everything in between.

Process 

- Talent Acquisition Interview (30' - 45')
- Hiring Manager Interview (45')
- Use Case (a live use case or one to be prepared at home and presented afterward)
- Meeting with the teams 
- 2 reference check

description:
About Voodoo

Voodoo is a consumer tech company founded in Paris in 2013, with one mission: entertain the world. Today we are 1,000 people, generating $1b+ in annual revenue, profitably. Our games and apps have passed 7 billion downloads and reach 200 million+ active users every month, making Voodoo the #3 mobile publisher worldwide in downloads, after Google and Meta. Team

As a French tech leader and global successful company, our Corporate teams are constantly looking for ways to innovate and increase organization efficiency to keep Voodoo ahead of the market. Voodoo’s Corporate function is composed of three teams: HR, Legal and Finance, working together to drive Voodoo’s success.

Role

We're looking for a Legal Counsel, AdTech Transactions to join our Legal team. In this role, you'll own the contracts and legal questions across Voodoo's advertising activity: selling ad inventory in our apps, buying user acquisition at scale, and the ad network we are now launching to connect third-party publishers and advertisers.

This position sits at the intersection of ad tech, commercial contracting, and data and privacy law, in a market where platform policies, ATT, GDPR, and consent frameworks change several times a year. Your work will directly shape how Voodoo monetizes its inventory, buys and measures user acquisition, grows its advertising network, and handles player data,while keeping us within legal and platform requirements and player expectations.

Your main responsibilities :

- Own ad tech transactions end-to-end for Voodoo's games and apps portfolio: draft, negotiate and close agreements with mediation platforms, ad networks, exchanges and SSPs on the sell side, and with ad networks, DSPs, direct advertisers and rewarded platforms on the buy side,including the incentive and rebate agreements (bonuses, UA credits, payment terms), that drive the commercial terms..

- Negotiate agreements with mobile measurement partners, attribution and analytics vendors, data providers and other partners

- Advise on SDK integrations and data flows together with the Privacy team, so contracts match what the tech actually does

- Build our advertising network's contract framework and advertising policies for third-party publishers, advertisers and programmatic partners; negotiate its infrastructure agreements and structure its commercial offers on the legal side

- Manage partner disputes with networks, mediation platforms and other ad tech partners, including reporting discrepancies, invalid traffic (IVT) and compensation claims, from first analysis through negotiated resolution.

- Track and apply platform policy changes and translate them into contract positions and business guidance

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Monetization, UA, Ad Network, Publishing and other product teams, serving as a trusted legal partner who helps the business move with speed and confidence

- Build scalable legal infrastructure-templates, playbooks, fallback positions, contract tooling - that allows the business to operate efficiently as volume grows

Profile

- 5-7 years of relevant legal experience, with meaningful time spent on ad tech and mobile/programmatic advertising, ideally in-house

- Substantive familiarity with ad tech: you understand how mediation, in-app bidding, SDK-based data collection, attribution and device identifiers work at a technical level - not just a conceptual one - and you know who does what along the supply chain

- Transactional experience: you've negotiated agreements with companies across the advertising ecosystem, ideally on both the publisher and advertiser side

- Privacy law fluency: you handle the privacy side of a deal as comfortably as the commercial side

- Industry standards: you know IAB terms and the TCF inside out

- Risk tolerance and business judgment: you're comfortable making calls in the absence of perfect information, offering clear and concise risk framing that avoids unnecessary stalling of the business. You operate like a business partner, not outside counsel

- Strong communication skills: you translate complex legal requirements into plain language for technical and non-technical stakeholders alike, and you're comfortable presenting your views succinctly and with confidence

- Autonomy and initiative: you take ownership of your portfolio, identify problems before they escalate, and propose solutions rather than waiting to be directed

- Master 2 in business law, IT/digital law or IP law from a French university or equivalent; avocat or in-house juriste profiles are equally welcome; an LL.M. or study abroad experience is a plus

- Full professional English required

description:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

- Coplan and execute discovery calls to understand customer requirements, their technical environment, and current business challenges.

- Design and execute repeatable Demo methodologies that prove Synthesia’s business value quickly, whether the customer is deploying Studio at scale, designing Roleplay Sessions for skill uplift, or integrating Interactive Avatars into their product.

- Develop and maintain reusable assets across demo environments, use cases, integration templates, objections, and industry playbooks brought to life directly in Synthesia’s platform.

- Support POC and pilot readouts as a business narrative, not a feature tour, learning to bring storytelling and executive presence to the room as you grow into more senior conversations.

- Provide technical guidance on platform capabilities, API and SDK integrations, security, compliance topics (SOC 2, GDPR, enterprise identity), and scalability for global deployments.

Product & Industry Expertise

- Stay ahead of the AI-native learning and enablement space, so you can credibly discuss how customers are shifting from current, static methods to interactive practice and measurable skill development.

Ecosystem Collaboration 

- Product: share customer and prospect feedback with Product, flagging pain points, missing capabilities, and gaps that surface in your deals to help shape the roadmap.

- Product Marketing: work with Product Marketing to understand and apply messaging and positioning in your deal cycles, and contribute to reusable assets like demo scripts and competitive battlecards.

- Customer Success: brief Customer Success on technical context and champion relationships at handover, so your POCs and pilots convert cleanly into production deployments.

- Enablement: Review and enhance enablement content from what is effective in preparing our team members for client engagements, delivering and evaluating certification as needed to accelerate understanding in the commercial team.

- Strong consultative discovery, stakeholder management, and communication skills, with the ability to engage credibly with both executive decision-makers (CHRO, CLO, Head of L&D, CTO) and technical audiences (IT, security, developers).

- Fluency with sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC and Command of the Message. Comfort translating technical requirements into business value and ROI conversations.

- Consultative approach to problem-solving; comfort gathering requirements, asking clarifying questions, and adapting solutions to customer needs.

- Excellent business and technical presentation skills, in person and remote, and the ability to explain complex AI and integration concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Self-motivated and organized; ability to manage multiple POCs, demos, and customer conversations simultaneously while meeting deadlines.

- Collaborative mindset; thrives working with AEs, Product, Customer Success, and other teams to drive customer and company success.

- Product orientation; genuine curiosity about how customers use technology

- Willing to travel; willingness to visit key customers for discovery, executive conversations, and on-site demos.

Location

Aiven is the open source based data platform that builders trust to run PostgreSQL®, Apache Kafka®, ClickHouse®, OpenSearch®, Valkey™ and more in production, on any cloud. Builders ship faster. Their companies run on data that stays available, secure + under control.

You are the technical owner of Aiven's strategic OEM partnerships, from the first pre-sales conversation to production at volume and beyond. OEM partners embed the Aiven platform inside their own products, so their architecture decisions become ours at scale: one design choice gets copied across hundreds of their customers. You win the technical evaluation, run the proof of concept, design the architecture, and stay on as the person both sides trust to say what should be built, what should be automated + what should be cut.

You work AI-native. Agents handle deployment analysis, usage monitoring, rightsizing, PoC scaffolding + first-draft documentation; your time goes on the judgment calls, the partner's engineers + the hard integration problems. You own how your work gets done and redesign it as the tools improve, without waiting for a playbook.

Life at Aiven 

Our values shape how we work. Get it done, together: we move with urgency, align on shared outcomes + put our effort where customers feel it most. Invent + impress: we challenge the status quo + bring different perspectives to hard problems. We commit + deliver: we own our commitments + do what we say.

In this role, that means working with Sales, Technical Account Managers, Product, Engineering + Support on every partner, being the person partners trust to follow through, and moving faster than the partner's other vendors. We know what needs doing; the risk is being slow.

Diverse perspectives make better ideas. Come as you are. We hire for how you think + what you can do.

What you will do 

Win the technical evaluation 

- Partner with Sales as the technical lead through the OEM sales cycle: discovery, architecture proposals, objection handling + commercial-technical trade-offs.

- Scope + run proofs of concept that answer the partner's real question, using agents to scaffold environments, generate test data + document results so the PoC takes days, not weeks.

Own the relationship + the resolution 

- Build trust-based relationships with partner engineering teams, technical decision makers + the Aiven sales reps you work alongside.

- Act as the technical liaison between partners and Product, Engineering + Support.

- When a partner is blocked, own it end-to-end across teams rather than handing it off.

- Close the loop fast: partner feedback becomes Product + Engineering tickets the same week, with evidence attached.

title: Senior Application Security Engineer
description:
About Nabla 

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure built for secure deployment across health systems.

About the Role 

We are scaling our healthcare AI platform, with more products, integrations and AI agents, and more protected health information (PHI) flowing through them. To keep pace, we're growing our security engineering team and looking for an exceptional Senior Security Engineer .

Our cloud infrastructure handles highly sensitive healthcare data, so security is core to everything we do. Our engineers already ask the right questions every day: can we use a one-time token here? How long should it live? How do we scope this OAuth Client?

You'll work directly with our Lead Security Engineer to bring real AppSec expertise into the product squads, and to strengthen security well beyond them.

This is a hands-on, high-impact role. About half your time goes to AppSec , but it is deliberately a broad security engineering role, not a pure code-review or pentest job. You'll regularly cross into platform and cloud, CI/CD and detection, and you'll own problems from start to finish. Code scanning, SCA and AI-driven code review are already running, but there is no AppSec process to undo. The threat-modeling practice, the security review loop, the triage rhythm and the secure-by-default libraries don't exist yet. You'll build them and run them.

If you're pragmatic, love working shoulder to shoulder with developers, and want your work to protect patients' most sensitive data, this role is for you.

Responsibilities 

- Partner with the product squads as their go-to security engineer: design reviews, per-feature threat modeling, and fast, opinionated answers on authN/authZ, tokens and session design.

- Secure our authentication and authorization surfaces (OAuth clients, one-time codes, multi-org tenancy, the Core API user API, embedded/postMessage SDKs) and hunt for BOLA, IDOR and broken access control before attackers do.

- Run the code-security findings loop: triage and prioritize results from our SAST, SCA, secrets and IaC scanners and AI-driven code review, route them to the right owners with SLAs, and drive the dependency-vulnerability backlog down, fixing issues yourself when that's faster.

- Secure our AI/LLM features and internal agents, covering prompt injection, tool and permission scoping for autonomous agents, PHI leakage, de-identification assurance and model/API egress.

- Run the external testing program: scope and run pentests (web, mobile, backoffice), validate fixes, operate our vulnerability disclosure program, and stand up a bug bounty.

- Build secure-by-default guardrails (secure coding guidelines, hardened libraries and patterns, pre-commit and PR checks) so the secure path is the easy path.

Qualifications 

- 5 to 8+ years in security engineering, including at least 2 to 3 years in application or product security, or experience as a software engineer with a strong security focus.

- Deep understanding of modern web and API security: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, session and token design, multi-tenancy, and the OWASP Top 10 and API Top 10. You can find access-control flaws by reading code.

- Strong coder, comfortable reading and fixing production code (mostly Kotlin and Python, plus web, mobile and desktop clients) and automating in Python.

- Experience running threat modeling and security design reviews, and operating SAST, SCA and secrets scanning in CI with a real triage loop, not just a dashboard.

- Genuine breadth: comfortable moving between an API design review, a supply-chain hardening PR and an incident in the same week, and honest about what you don't know yet.

- Excellent communicator who earns developers' trust and works well with engineering, compliance and IT.

- Full professional fluency in French and English (oral and written).

Nice to have: LLM / AI agent security, mobile app security, pentest or bug bounty experience, GCP / GKE, or experience in healthcare or another regulated industry.

When you join Nabla, you join a team that is driven by excellence, curiousity, and kindness. Together, we’re committed to making clinicians’ lives easier and improving healthcare experiences for everyone. We believe clinicians should be able to focus on what they were trained to do, caring for their patients, and that no patient should feel their visit was rushed. 

We work hard and make time to have fun, too. Our #nablabla channel is just as active as #feature-show-off . We also host regular off-sites, meet up across New York, Paris, San Francisco, and other cities, and keep the chocolate and nuts well stocked.

If this sounds like an environment where you’ll thrive, we look forward to reading your application.

Our Values at Nabla 

Joining Nabla means being part of a team that shares a commitment to excellence, humility, growth, and inclusion.

Every day is a new chance to excel 

We aim for nothing less than the best and are willing to put in the effort and dedication required to exceed standards. We learn from yesterday’s failures and do better every day.

Stay humble

title: Director, Luxury Market Intelligence & Insights
description:
We are growing! We are currently looking to hire a Director, Luxury Market Intelligence & Insights . 

About CXG: 

Founded in 2006, CXG is a global customer experience company uniquely positioned at the intersection of data-driven retail performance, customer experience transformation, and operational execution across 200+ luxury brands worldwide.

The mission of our 270 collaborators is to help brands transform customer and employee experiences through tailored insights, strategy, and implementation.

We are passionate about delivering impact.

Our clients include the world's most admired luxury houses, and our solutions combine research, technology, and human expertise to elevate every customer interaction.

We are looking for a thought leadership expert with the editorial vision to spot what matters next, the conviction to shape CXG's point of view, and the writing talent to make it influential across luxury retail, beauty and cosmetics, watches and jewellery, automotive, and hospitality.

Context and role 

Reporting to the Chief of Staff, you will lead CXG's Thought Leadership and Market Intelligence functions. You will define the topics on which CXG should have a distinctive and credible point of view, turn CXG's proprietary data, expertise and market knowledge into original external content, and position the company ahead of emerging developments in customer experience, luxury and its priority verticals.

This is a hands-on role: you will research, analyse, write and produce content yourself, while mobilising expertise and data from across the business. You will be accountable for ensuring that every publication presents a recognisable CXG angle rather than simply reporting market developments or repeating established industry views. You will manage one Market Intelligence team member.

Thought Leadership Development 

- Define the thought leadership strategy and roadmap, including priority themes, target audiences, formats and a realistic publication calendar.
- Drive and coordinate content creation across Practices, Solutions and Regions.
- Work closely with Practices, Regions and Solutions to: 
- Push: scan for trends and hot topics and ensure CXG has a voice and perspective, commenting regularly on these subjects.
- Pull: identify and collect new ideas and proposed topics from the relevant stakeholders, prioritise and incorporate them into the thought leadership roadmap.
- Use market intelligence, CXG's proprietary data, internal expertise and client-facing insights to identify emerging topics early, develop a clear CXG point of view and decide where CXG can make a credible contribution to the conversation.
- Research, interview internal experts, write and edit articles, perspectives and other thought leadership content directly. Challenge generic claims and ensure each piece advances a clear argument and is supported by credible evidence.
- Ensure that analysis is methodologically sound, appropriately contextualised and presented without compromising client confidentiality.
- Develop topics that connect expertise across Practices and Regions, while reflecting relevant differences between markets.
Thought Leadership Communication 

- Ensure relevant thought leadership pieces (e.g., perspectives, publications) are disseminated on a periodic basis.
- Work with Marketing on the publication, distribution and promotion of content, while retaining ownership of the editorial strategy, substance, quality and consistency of CXG's point of view. In addition, collaborate with Marketing to maximise impact by communicating through the channels relevant to each market.
- Track the reach, engagement and qualitative response generated by CXG's thought leadership, as well as relevant business enquiries influenced by published content. Use the findings to refine the roadmap.
- Shape and host or contribute to CXG's podcast "The Luxury Edit", working with internal experts and guests to develop topics, prepare interviews and turn conversations into useful content.
- Develop the content and key messages for CXG-hosted events and external conferences, panels and talks; act as a CXG speaker where appropriate; and work with internal experts to prepare other CXG speakers and turn the company's point of view into compelling presentations and discussion topics.
- Look for and test new thought leadership formats (e.g., interactive reports, data visualisations, short-form video, newsletters, social-first content) to broaden reach, engage new audiences and keep CXG's content distinctive.
- Identify and build collaborations with conferences, specialised industry magazines and universities (e.g., content partnerships, guest articles, co-branded publications, joint research, guest lectures, speaking slots) to extend CXG's visibility and credibility with target audiences.
Market Intelligence 

- Keep abreast of market and competitive developments and ensure relevant findings are communicated across CXG.
- Translate these findings into clear implications for CXG's strategic priorities, client conversations, commercial opportunities and external thought leadership.
- Contribute market intelligence, evidence and relevant CXG perspectives to priority proposals and client deliverables, working with Practices, Solutions and Regions to strengthen the quality and relevance of the final output.
- Manage and develop the Market Intelligence team member, setting clear priorities and reviewing the quality and usefulness of their work.
Competitive Analysis 

- Develop and continuously update a list of CXG competitors.
- Research competitor performance, including revenues and market share where reliable information is available.
- Identify and assess the impact of new competitors' offerings.
- Review competitors' thought leadership, influence and presence.
- Identify gaps in the conversations competitors are leading and opportunities for CXG to establish a distinct position.
Industry Analysis 

- Research and review clients' developments (e.g., new strategy, launch of new product or service, restructuring, M&A, key managerial appointments).
- Track public financial announcements (e.g., quarterly and annual earnings).
- Monitor developments in luxury, retail, customer experience and adjacent sectors; distinguish lasting shifts from short-lived topics and explain their implications for CXG and its clients.
- Publish the weekly "This Week in Luxury" news brief and issue timely flash updates when significant developments require immediate attention, such as financial announcements, major transactions or leadership changes.
Internal Dissemination and Application 

- Synthesise research and findings into concise, actionable outputs tailored to the needs of relevant internal stakeholders. Feed findings into the Thought Leadership roadmap.
- Proactively bring relevant market signals to Practices, Regions and leadership early enough to inform decisions, client conversations and potential cross-practice opportunities.
- Disseminate new thought leadership across CXG and equip Practices, Regions and client-facing teams with the key messages and supporting materials needed to use it in client conversations and commercial activities.
Requirements 

What will you bring along? 

- Proven experience developing thought leadership, editorial content or insight-led communications in a consulting, research, customer experience, retail or luxury environment.
- Excellent English writing and editing skills, with a portfolio demonstrating original, well-argued, evidence-led articles or publications written personally. If possible, include examples that turn proprietary research, data or specialist expertise into a distinctive point of view. Additional languages (e.g., French, Mandarin) are a plus.
- Strong oral communication and presentation skills, with the confidence to represent CXG as a speaker at conferences, panels and client events.
- Proven ability to build relationships and influence senior stakeholders across functions and regions without direct authority.
- An established network or demonstrated ability to build partnerships with media, conference organisers, academic institutions or industry bodies.
- Comfort working with quantitative data and research methods, and the ability to translate data into clear, credible narratives and visualisations.
- Ability to define and track content performance indicators and use them to refine editorial priorities.
- Strong research and analytical skills: able to assess sources critically, connect market signals and form a clear point of view rather than simply summarise trends.
- Familiarity with AI-assisted research and content tools, used with appropriate rigour.
- Sound knowledge of luxury, retail and customer experience, and curiosity about how these sectors are evolving across markets.
- Ability to interview senior experts, challenge ideas constructively and turn specialist knowledge into accessible, credible content.
- Comfort working independently in a remote setting, managing an editorial roadmap and delivering finished work without a large production team.
- Experience managing or coaching at least one team member.
- Confidence preparing and hosting interviews or podcasts is a plus.

Qui sommes-nous: 

Burson, leader mondial de la communication, a pour mission de créer de la valeur pour ses clients par la gestion de leur réputation. Grâce à notre expertise, nos technologies de pointe, nos solutions d'intelligence artificielle et notre créativité, nous anticipons les risques en temps réel, identifions les insights générateurs de préférence et d'engagement, et accompagnons la transformation et la réussite de nos clients. Nous réinventons la réputation pour en faire un véritable atout concurrentiel. Burson est le gardien de votre réputation, le partenaire qui vous guide dans un environnement complexe.

En rejoignant Burson, vous intégrez une communauté mondiale d'experts à la pointe de l'innovation.

Burson fait partie du groupe WPP (LSE/NYSE : WPP), spécialiste de la transformation créative. Pour en savoir plus, rendez-vous sur bursonglobal.com et suivez-nous sur LinkedIn et Instagram .

En savoir plus sur le rôle: 

Vous intégrerez l’équipe Crise & Affaires Publiques de l’agence, composée d’une dizaine de consultant.es, pour participer à leurs côtés à la gestion des affaires publiques (relations institutionnelles et lobbying) et des situations sensibles ou de crise, de clients de secteurs très divers.

Si l’équipe rassemble deux expertises, ce poste aura une majeure en Affaires Publiques. 

Vos missions 

- Affaires publiques : Superviser la veille institutionnelle, législative et réglementaire ; identifier et mobiliser les parties prenantes clés ; élaborer des argumentaires stratégiques (position papers, amendements) ; concevoir et piloter des actions de lobbying et d'influence.

- Création de contenus & excellence rédactionnelle : Production de contenus à haute valeur ajoutée (tribunes, communiqués de presse stratégiques, prises de parole de dirigeants, livres blancs, mémoires institutionnels) et garantir l'excellence rédactionnelle de l'équipe.

- Communication de crise : Concevoir et piloter les stratégies de gestion et communication de crise ; analyser et cartographier les risques ; superviser les dispositifs de veille médias et réseaux sociaux pour analyser les tendances et signaux faibles, traduire les opportunités/menaces en recommandations stratégiques directement exploitables par nos clients et rédiger des messages clés et éléments de langage adaptés. 

- Pilotage de comptes, management & new business : Assurer le suivi opérationnel et financier des projets (gestion des budgets, rentabilité), encadrer et faire monter en compétences les consultants juniors et alternants ; participer activement aux réflexions stratégiques de l’équipe/agence ; réponses aux appels d'offres et soutenances commercial.

Et bien plus encore !

Profil recherché 

- Expérience : Vous justifiez de 4 à 6 ans d’expérience en cabinet de conseil en Affaires Publique, en agence de communication ou au sein de la Direction de la communication/Affaires Publiques d'une entreprise.

- Formation : Formation Bac +5 (IEP / Sciences Po, Droit public / Affaires Publiques, CELSA, Grande École de Commerce).

- Expertise : Solides compétences en Affaires Publiques requises ; expériences en communication de crise et gestion de la réputation corporate appréciées.

- Posture conseil & analyse : Esprit d'analyse aiguisé, forte curiosité pour l'actualité et les enjeux de société, et capacité à transformer des problématiques complexes en recommandations concrètes et impactantes pour des dirigeants.

- Qualités rédactionnelles : Plume soignée et maîtrise des exigences de production de contenus stratégiques.

- Organisation & leadership : Autonomie, rigueur, excellente gestion des priorités et capacité à animer des équipes projets en environnement exigeant et dynamique.

- Langues : Maîtrise parfaite du français à l’écrit comme à l’oral et capacité à travailler quotidiennement en anglais (écrit et oral) dans un contexte international.

- 
Un environnement stimulant : Intégrez une agence reconnue mondialement, au cœur des stratégies de communication des plus grandes marques.

Une expérience professionnalisante : Développez des compétences clés et construisez une carrière solide dans un secteur en constante évolution.

Une culture d’entreprise forte : Rejoignez une équipe dynamique et collaborative.

-

- 
14 jours de RTT par an.

- 
Accès aux avantages du Comité d’Entreprise (cinéma, chèques cadeaux, remboursements sportifs…).

title: Head of Security
description:
About Morpho

Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here .

Location:

Paris or remote (from -5h GMT up to +2h GMT to ensure sufficient overlap with the rest of the team).

About the role:

As Head of Security, you'll define and drive Morpho's security strategy across the entire organization - corporate IT, cloud and infrastructure, application, supply chain, identity, incident response, threat intelligence, and counterparty security - and you'll build the team and function to deliver it. This is a hands-on leadership role: in the early days you'll personally do the work while you hire, and you'll stay close enough to the technical detail to earn the trust of a deeply technical organization. You'll also be Morpho's credible security voice, internally to leadership, and externally to the integrators, institutions, and ecosystem partners who depend on us. You'll partner closely with Engineering on infrastructure and deployment integrity, and with our Integration team, which works with various partners across the Morpho ecosystem.

Responsibilities:

- Own and continuously evolve Morpho's security strategy and roadmap across, cloud/infrastructure, application, supply-chain, identity, and operational security.

- Build and lead the security function - hire, grow, and develop the team, recruiting skillsets across security operations and application security.

- Oversight of the IT function

- Stay hands-on. Personally execute critical security work - threat modeling, architecture review, control implementation, and incident command - while the team scales.

- Set the governance architecture: a coherent security framework that ties tooling and controls together, rather than accumulating tools in isolation.

- Own incident response end to end - runbooks, incident command, severity and escalation structure, and market communication during an event.

- Build and run a counterparty security program for curators and partners - identity verification, screening, operational diligence, and bidirectional incident-coordination channels.

- Lead Morpho's certification strategy (e.g. SOC 2, ISO 27001), meeting both the spirit and the letter sustainably.

- Represent Morpho's security posture externally - to fintechs, financial institutions, and the broader ecosystem - and internally to executives.

- Partner cross-functionally with Engineering, Protocol, and Integrations, driving security outcomes through both direct ownership and influence.

What Success Looks Like:

First 30 Days

- You've built a clear, independent picture of Morpho's posture, architecture, threat model, and in-flight work - and pressure-tested the existing strategy against it.

- You've met the team and established working relationships with the people who own the surfaces you'll most depend on.

- You understand the path-to-funds attack surface in depth and have an early, evidence-based view of the highest-severity risks and quick wins.

- You know exactly where incident-response readiness stands today.

First 60 Days

- You've published a clearly prioritized security roadmap with clear sequencing, owners, and the rationale for what's deferred and aligned leadership behind it.

- You've defined the team build-out plan and opened the first hire.

- You're personally driving the top-severity gaps - identity and authentication enforcement, deployment guardrails, and a documented incident-response runbook among them.

- You've set the governance framework and the certification path in motion.

First 90 Days

- Demonstrable progress closing the highest-priority gaps, with key controls enforced rather than optional.

- A documented incident-response capability that's been validated by at least one tabletop exercise.

- Hiring underway, and a clear operating rhythm established with Engineering, Protocol, and Integrations.

- Morpho's external security posture is taking shape - trust surface, counterparty security program, and ecosystem engagement - and you're recognized internally and externally as Morpho's credible security voice.

Must-have Experience & Skills:

- 10+ years in security, several of them building or leading a security function, ideally at a crypto/web3, fintech, or financial-services company where security is core to the business.

- Strong grasp of the crypto/web3 threat model

- Proven experience building and growing a security team from a small base, recruiting across security operations and application/infrastructure security.

- Deep, hands-on technical expertise across cloud, infrastructure, CI/CD, supply-chain, identity, and application security - you do the work, not just direct it.

- Owned incident response end to end, including incident command and external communication.

- Sharp prioritization and the ability to galvanize action through hard and soft influence, including driving outcomes through teams you don't own.

- Exceptional, organized, responsive communication - credible to executives and to external audiences from fintechs to Fortune 500 institutions.

- Humble.

Nice to Have:

- An established network and public profile in the security or crypto-security community, and comfort representing security work publicly (talks, writing, framework contribution).

- Offensive security depth, or experience standing up red/blue capabilities.

- Familiarity with institutional and regulatory expectations and threat-sharing networks (e.g. Crypto ISAC, TIBER-style frameworks).

- Taken an organization through certifications (SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent)

Perks & Benefits

We design benefits around deep work and growth, so you can do the best work of your career. Expect fair, top-tier compensation, real flexibility, time together in Paris, great health coverage, and support to keep learning.

Equal Opportunity

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and hire based on talent, potential, and values alignment.
